transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
Former Congresswoman Mary Peltola is returning to Washington, this time as the senator from
Alaska.
She is unseated incumbent Dan Sullivan, according to a race call by the Associated Press.
It's the latest Republican-held seat seized by Democrats this election cycle, impairs
Eric McDaniel reports.
Peltola ran a campaign squarely centered on Alaskan issues, fish, family, and freedom.
The moderate Democrat previously served in Congress as Alaska's sole house member.
Her Senate race was a controversial one.
The New York Times spoke to a former campaign staffer who alleged Democrats recruited a
man with the same name as her opponent into the race.
She denies involvement, and NPR has not independently confirmed the allegations.
Peltola's race is the final Senate race to be called.
Democrats will control the chamber 56 to 44.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News in Washington.
>> President Trump is in Manila for a regional summit, and next heads to Shenzhen, China for
more high-stakes meetings, NPR's Deepa Shivram reports.
>> Analysts say it's significant that Trump met with US allies like India, Japan, and
Australia before he heads to China for meetings with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's
Vladimir Putin.
The president emphasized the importance of alliances with democracies in the Pacific
region, and he signed a trade deal with Thailand.
The next stop for Trump is Shenzhen, the high-tech city that neighbors Hong Kong.
It's where Xi is hosting a large economic summit.
This is Trump's first trip abroad since his party lost control of the next Congress.
Trump's priorities with allies and adversaries, including discussions on the Iran war and
Russia's war in Ukraine, are being closely watched.
Deepa Shivram, NPR News, Shenzhen.
>> Secretary of State Marco Rubio seeking to reassure the American public about the
spate of tech issues that have led to snarled airports and affected banking, national security,
and email.
Traveling with President Trump, Rubio said there is zero information that the service
outages are related to each other.
Britain says it's imposing sanctions on Israeli companies involved in building settlements
in the occupied West Bank and in blocking aid to Gaza.
NPR's Lauren Prayer reports Israel calls the move a hostile act.
Back in September, Britain's Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced a toughening of policy
toward Israel, and now he's given details.
The sanctions target eight Israeli construction companies, along with an activist group Britain
says has blocked aid to Gaza.
They'll be cut off from the British financial system barred from doing business in Britain
and have any British assets frozen.
Miliband says illegal Israeli settlements threatened the two-state solution.
His Israeli counterpart Gideon Saar calls these sanctions a hostile act, targeting private
law-abiding companies, and he accuses Britain of bias and hostility.
Saar says Israel will consider new ways to strengthen those settlements in response.
Lauren Prayer, NPR News, in Ramallah in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
New York Attorney General Letitia James has formally challenged the revised petition to
remove her from the Cornell rape investigation.
Ellie Oskara with member station WAMC reports.
>> In a memo filed Monday in State Supreme Court, attorneys representing the attorney
general pushed back against a petition signed by five students accused of sexual assault
in the 2024 incident at Cornell University.
The petition revolves around a social media post, James wrote, saying, quote, "What this
young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable."
The state's memo argues the petition still has flaws, namely other defendants in the
Jane Doe litigation were left out of the petition but could still be found criminally liable.
They also argued that since Jane Doe's case is in Tompkins County, the petition should
be filed there instead of Albany County.
For NPR News, I'm Elias Oskara.
>> Nvidia has rejected Jensen Huang's offer to return as the company's chief executive.
The chairman, Harvey Jones, said at the start of a quarterly earnings call today that the
company's board had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and does not intend to reinstate
him.
Huang stepped down last week amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one with
a suspected Chinese spy.
The end of the two-month criminal trial of China's Huawei Technologies is near, a jury
in Brooklyn is likely to begin deliberations Wednesday.
After two days of closing arguments, prosecutors call Huawei a criminal enterprise that helped
Iran spy on its citizens and steal from U.S. companies.
The defense says prosecutors have been spending a false narrative.
This is NPR News.
